about.title: Belmont Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: A wrongful death case begins with something no family wants to face — the loss of a spouse, parent, or child because of someone else's carelessness on the road. Belmont's collision data shows dozens of injury crashes each year along corridors like US-101, Old County Road, and Ralston Avenue, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. seeing the heaviest reporting. While the city's most recent final numbers show zero traffic deaths for that period, San Mateo County families still turn to wrongful death claims after fatal crashes on local roads, at intersections, or involving negligent drivers passing through town. These civil claims exist separately from any criminal charges and focus on the financial and emotional toll left behind. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply help connect grieving families in Belmont with an independent, contingency-based attorney so they can understand their options without added financial pressure during an already difficult time.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Wrongful Death Claim

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California law limits standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. An attorney can help clarify where your family fits before any steps are taken.

items.title: A Strict Filing Deadline
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing this deadline can close the door on recovery entirely.

items.title: Losses That Can Be Considered
items.desc: California allows families to seek recovery for funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's losses look different, and an attorney can help identify what applies to yours.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action focused on financial and emotional losses, while any criminal case against the at-fault party is handled independently by prosecutors. Families can pursue a civil claim regardless of the outcome of a criminal matter.

items.question: Belmont's recent crash data shows zero traffic deaths — does that mean wrongful death claims don't apply here?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Crash data reflects a specific reporting period, and fatal incidents can still occur on Belmont roads like El Camino Real or near busy corridors during other periods. If a family in Belmont has lost a loved one due to another's negligence, a wrongful death claim may still be worth exploring.

items.question: How long do we have to take action after losing a family member?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though this window shortens significantly if a government entity is involved. Because evidence and witness memories fade over time, reaching out sooner rather than later is usually recommended.
